stories.title: S. Carolina Aquarium Celebrates 'Baby Boom' of Critically-Endangered Penguin Chicks
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: An aquarium in Myrtle Beach just welcomed five new African penguin chicks, joining two others born earlier this year for a record-breaking season. African penguins are critically endangered, so every new chick is a real boost for the species' survival. The aquarium's care team has been carefully managing breeding pairs to help build a healthy, growing colony. It's a sweet reminder that dedicated zookeepers and aquariums can make a real difference for animals in trouble. Seven fuzzy new penguin babies is about as good as good news gets.
stories.why_good: A real, verified increase in a critically endangered species' population thanks to conservation work, with no suffering or controversy involved.

stories.title: 22-yo with Down Syndrome Becomes Certified Fitness Instructor, Leads Class of 60 at Local Gym
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A 22-year-old woman in Utah named Aubry Allbridge just became a fully certified fitness instructor for a popular barre program. Her gym co-owner had noticed her passion and drive over the years and encouraged her to go for it. Aubry recently led her very first class, guiding a room of 60 people through a workout with confidence. It's a wonderful reminder that with the right support, people with Down Syndrome can lead, teach, and inspire others in ways big and small.
stories.why_good: It's a real, already-happened achievement that shows inclusion in action, with no suffering at its core, just a young woman succeeding at something she worked hard for.

stories.title: FDA Immediately Approves Drug That's Doubling Lifespan for Late Pancreatic Cancer Patients
stories.label: health
stories.summary: The FDA has just approved a new twice-daily pill for people with advanced pancreatic cancer, one of the toughest cancers to treat. In trials, patients taking it lived roughly twice as long as those who didn't, even after standard chemotherapy had stopped working. Pancreatic cancer survival rates have been stuck at painfully low numbers for decades, so a treatment that meaningfully extends life is a huge step forward. Doctors are hopeful this gives patients and families more precious time together.
stories.why_good: A real, already-approved drug is measurably doubling survival time for patients with one of the deadliest cancers.
